feat: Styxy v2 — rewrite as LD_PRELOAD transparent port resolver

Replace the entire v1 daemon-based architecture (~4,500 lines JS) with a
minimal LD_PRELOAD library (~200 lines C) and Rust CLI (~280 lines).

Styxy now hooks libc bind() transparently. On EADDRINUSE, it finds the
nearest free port, rebinds, and prints an LLM-readable notification to
stderr. No daemon, no state, no config required.

Security hardening: constructor-time init (thread-safe), bounded /proc
walk, dprintf instead of fprintf, addrlen overflow guard, passthrough
lists for ports and programs that need EADDRINUSE to fail normally.

10/10 tests passing.

## Phase 2 Implementation Complete
- Created ~/lib/styxy-intercept.c (370 lines of C code)
- Implemented bind() interceptor using dlsym(RTLD_NEXT, "bind")
- Built custom HTTP client using raw sockets (no libcurl dependency)
- Integrated with Styxy daemon APIs (/observe, /suggest, /register-instance)

- Only intercepts IPv4 TCP sockets on user ports (>= 1024)

docs: Complete port 8000 allocation failure root cause analysis

Investigated port conflict during MFA testing and identified performance
optimization creating coordination bypass vulnerability.

## Investigation Results
- Root cause: Managed range optimization (daemon.js:1130-1132) skips OS checks
- Port 8000 in "api" managed range [8000-8099] allows external process bypass
- Python demo server bound directly without Styxy allocation request
- Verified: NOT a Styxy bug - conflict detection works when invoked

## Key Findings
- Performance optimization assumes all managed range usage goes through Styxy
- External processes (npm, Python, Docker) can bypass coordination
- Current design trades some safety for 98% performance improvement (3s → 25ms)
- Conflict detection feature operational and correctly implemented

## Deliverables
- REMEDIATION_REPORT_PORT_8000.md: Comprehensive root cause analysis
- Hybrid safety model recommendations (short and long-term)
- Integration guidance for external processes
- Updated CURRENT_STATUS.md and HANDOFF_PROMPT.md with findings

## Status
- System verified healthy (daemon running, port now available)
- Architecture trade-off documented (performance vs external coordination)
- Recommendations provided for enhanced safety without breaking changes
